input: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Top line is still shrinking: ending Paid Connected Fitness subs 2.475M, down 9% Y/Y at Q1 FY27, with Q2 guided down 9% Y/Y at midpoint and FY27 revenue guided down ~4% - the turnaround is profitability-first, not growth
Churn rose to 2.2% average net monthly in Q4 FY26 (vs 1.2% in Q3 and 1.8% a year earlier) after subscription price increases; Citi cut its PT citing rising customer turnover

Q1 FY27's 61.3% gross margin was 'partially driven by nonrecurring benefits' and Q2 FY27 gross margin is guided back to ~50.0% with Adjusted EBITDA guided to $85-100M vs $167.8M in Q1 - the EBITDA run-rate is seasonally and structurally lumpier than the latest print
Litigation: a $23.8M nonrecurring accrued legal contingency for patent litigation hit Q4 FY26 Adjusted EBITDA, and a securities class action appeal (No. 24-2803) remains pending at the Second Circuit

10-K risk factors: tariffs and changes in global trade policy, reliance on a limited number of suppliers/contract manufacturers, and product safety/recalls (Original Series Bike and Bike+ seat post recalls) could disrupt hardware economics

Balance sheet still carries a $139.7M stockholders' deficit and heavy share-count growth (Class A +32M Y/Y), so equity upside is diluted and convertible notes ($344.9M net, conversion price ~$4.58) are in the money at ~$5.78

Refinancing execution risk: the $600M senior secured notes' interest rate is not yet set, Bloomberg characterized the deal as a first-time junk-bond tap, and management flagged credit-market volatility since late August - terms could come at a higher cost of capital than the term loan being replaced

catalysts.claim: Peloton launched a private offering of $600.0 million senior secured notes due 2032 plus a proposed $200.0 million five-year revolving credit facility; pricing and closing in the coming months is the most immediate catalyst, with the interest rate and terms to be set at pricing
Peloton Commercial Series Bike and Tread are set to launch in Q2 FY2027 (October-December 2026 quarter), extending the commercial business that grew revenue double digits Y/Y in FY26

Q2 FY2027 earnings expected early February 2027 (prior-year quarter was reported 2026-02-05); management guides Q2 FY27 revenue $625-650M, gross margin ~50.0%, Adjusted EBITDA $85-100M, ending subs 2.425-2.445M

Pending Second Circuit decision in the securities class action (No. 24-2803, class period Feb 5 2021 - Jan 19 2022); district court dismissed with prejudice 2024-09-30 and appellants' brief was filed 2025-01-28
Management has guided to new products in new categories in Fall 2027 (new products in existing categories, the September 22 2026 Tread lineup, delivered in Fall 2026)

event_driven.claim: Structuring of the new $600M notes offering explicitly contemplates strategic options: remaining net proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes possibly including share repurchases, capital expenditures, working capital and acquisitions
Peloton completed the acquisition of Skop, an early innovator in Connected Pilates (FY26 business combinations spend $11.4M, also including Breathwrk closed in Q1 FY26)
Strategic partnership with Spotify (launched April 2026) expanding Peloton's global digital reach
CFO Liz Coddington departed at end of March 2026; Siddharth (Sid) Thacker is now CFO - a completed management transition that removes a prior overhang
Activist Blackwells Capital (~5% stake in 2022) publicly urged Peloton to sell itself; no current activist campaign was found as of 2026-11-10

output.research_view: Peloton's story has flipped from survival to a cost-driven turnaround: FY26 delivered its first full-year net income ($63M) and $378M FCF, Q1 FY27 beat on every line ($559.2M revenue, 61.3% gross margin, $167.8M EBITDA), and net debt has gone negative with a $600M secured-notes refi launched 2026-11-09 to cut the cost of capital further. What matters most now is (1) the pricing and terms of that refinancing, (2) whether the ~9% Y/Y subscriber decline and 2.2% churn stabilize as FY27 revenue is guided down ~4%, and (3) whether commercial/microstore expansion and the Q2 FY27 Commercial Series launch can become a real second growth leg. The stock ($5.78 on 2026-11-10) trades on the durability of cost-driven EBITDA against a shrinking top line, with converts due 2029 already in the money and adding dilution risk.

credit_signals.claim: New global refinancing: $600.0M senior secured notes due 2032 plus a proposed $200.0M five-year revolving credit facility; proceeds plus cash will repay all term loans under the existing $1.0B term loan facility, which will be terminated on repayment; first-time high-yield ('junk bond') market tap and first ratings process, per Bloomberg/CFO Sid Thacker

Voluntarily repaid $280M of the Term Loan after the Q1 FY27 close; gross principal debt $1.048B, down 32% from $1.534B at 2025-12-31; cash $1,342.2M exceeded total debt $1,298.9M at 2026-09-30, putting net debt negative

As of 2026-06-30: Total Debt $1.3B, Net Debt $93M (down $367M or 80% Y/Y); cash and equivalents $1,206.6M; term loan net of current portion $944.2M; convertible notes net of current portion $344.9M; current portion of debt only $10.0M

5.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029: $300.0M priced 2024-05-21, maturing 2029-12-01, not redeemable before 2027-06-07, conversion price ~$4.58/share - versus a $5.78 close on 2026-11-10, the converts are in the money
0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026-02-15 were repaid at maturity during FY2026 ($199.0M convertible notes principal repaid in FY26); Term Loan due 2029-05-30 remains outstanding

Debt service remains the largest cash cost: FY26 interest expense $123.8M (Q4 $30.0M); cash paid for interest $122.2M; the refinancing aims to lower the cost of capital, but benefit depends on final terms since the note rate is not yet set

missing_fields: S&P/Moody's issuer ratings or rating actions for PTON (company disclosed it is undergoing its first ratings process; no agency action page was found)
Consensus EPS estimate for Q1 FY2027 (only guidance comparisons confirmed)
Current 13D/13G filings as of November 2026 (only >10% holder identified was Morgan Stanley, per a January 2025 court disclosure)
Annual meeting date from the DEF 14A filed 2026-10-23 (proxy not opened)
Annual meeting date from the DEF 14A filed 2026-10-23 (proxy not opened); no index changes or lock-up expiries found for the next 6 months

alternative_signals.claim: Peloton cut ~11% of its workforce on 2026-01-30, primarily engineering/technology teams - the second cut in five months, after an August 2025 ~6% cut tied to a $100M cost-savings plan

US headcount fell to 1,736 in June 2026 from ~6,700 in June 2021; cumulative severance/personnel charges of $259.2M under restructuring plans; plans substantially completed as of 2026-06-30 with no material additional charges expected

Product cadence: launched foldable Peloton Tread Flex - its most affordable treadmill ever - plus Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision, Peloton IQ AI coaching (Run Analysis, IQ Pace Targets, ReRuns) and WHOOP integration; 'Let Yourself Run' campaign with Miley debuted late September 2026

Commercial Business Unit revenue grew double digits Y/Y; ten additional US microstores opened since the start of Q1 FY27 (19 total), with a plan to double the microstore fleet in FY27 - distribution expansion beyond the home

Pricing changes: Cross Training Series hardware refresh and higher hardware and subscription prices announced 2025-10-01; churn stayed elevated thereafter (1.9% in Q2 FY26, 2.2% in Q4 FY26 vs 1.2% in Q3 FY26)
Channel/sell-side check: on 2025-11-20 Citi analyst Ronald Josey cut the PT to $8.25 from $9.50 (Neutral), lowering the subscriber forecast 3% after Q1 FY26 due to a rise in customer turnover

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-09-30): revenue $559.2M, up 2% Y/Y and $4M above the midpoint of the $545-565M guidance range - a revenue beat
Q1 FY2027 GAAP net income $96.2M (vs $13.9M a year earlier); Adjusted EBITDA $167.8M, up 42% Y/Y and above the $135-145M guidance range

Q1 FY2027 total gross margin 61.3%, up 975 bps Y/Y and above the ~57% guidance, partially driven by nonrecurring benefits; Free Cash Flow $143.4M, up 113%; ending Paid Connected Fitness subs 2.475M, down 9% Y/Y, at the top of the guidance range

Current guidance: Q2 FY2027 revenue $625-650M (down 3% Y/Y at midpoint), gross margin ~50.0%, Adjusted EBITDA $85-100M, ending subs 2.425-2.445M (down 9% Y/Y at midpoint); full-year FY2027 outlook unchanged: revenue $2.30-2.40B (down 4% Y/Y at midpoint), gross margin ~54.0%, Adjusted EBITDA $475-525M, Free Cash Flow at least $350M

Q4 FY2026 (reported 2026-08-06): revenue $607.7M, roughly flat Y/Y; FY26 revenue $2.446B, $6M above the guidance range on equipment outperformance (Peloton and Precor); gross margin in line with guidance; FY26 Adjusted EBITDA $468M (+16% Y/Y); FY26 GAAP net income $63M - first full year of net profitability in company history; FY26 FCF $378M (+17%)

Q3 FY2026: revenue $630.9M beat the $605-625M guidance range and $618.7M consensus, up 1% Y/Y; raised FY26 revenue guidance to $2.42-2.44B and FCF guidance to ~$350M; gross margin 51.9% missed ~54% guidance on opportunistic promotional activity

Q2 FY2026: revenue $656.5M missed the $675.0M consensus by $18.5M and company guidance by ~$8M (fewer equipment upgrades, ~$4M delivery delays); EPS -$0.09 vs -$0.07 consensus; FY26 revenue guidance cut by $30M; stock fell nearly 25% on the miss and CFO departure news

Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended 2025-09-30): revenue $550.8M, down ~6% Y/Y, and net income $13.9M - a return to profitability that beat expectations; shares surged more than 11% after hours and management raised FY26 Adjusted EBITDA and net income guidance

insider_and_ownership.claim: 4 insiders sold $1.2M of PTON on the open market in the last 90 days; no open-market purchases
Saqib Baig (Chief Accounting Officer) sold 10,000 shares at $5.45 ($54,500) on 2026-10-20 under a 10b5-1 plan, holding 257,729 direct shares
Charles Peter Kirol (COO) exercised 56,510 options and sold 28,849 shares at $5.33 ($154K) on 2026-10-15
Dion C. Sanders (Chief Commercial Officer) sold 112,512 shares at $5.45 ($613K) on 2026-08-19 under a 10b5-1 plan; director Karen Boone sold 25,000 shares at ~$5.35 on 2026-08-17

Large option grants at $0 exercise price to senior executives on 2026-09-07: CEO Peter Stern 2,151,221 shares; COO Kirol 598,887; CAO Baig 339,749; CPO Caldwell 273,623 - a major incentive reload tied to the turnaround

Morgan Stanley held more than 10% of Peloton's Class A common stock per its court-filed corporate disclosure statement (most recent >10% institutional holding identified); no current 13D/13G filing was opened for this run
Share count growth (dilution): Class A shares rose to 422,802,650 at 2026-06-30 from 390,579,270 a year earlier (Class B constant at 15,836,724)
